regions._comment: Region view groups stops by landmark. It is the default when a page has more than autoThreshold stops. A landmark with more than maxStopsPerRegion stops is split into inferred groups (lists, named containers) of at least minGroupStops. 'Long jumps only' hides arrows shorter than longJumpPx unless they jump backwards.

safari._comment: By default Safari's Tab key only reaches text fields and pop-up menus (plus elements with tabindex); links, buttons, checkboxes and similar are skipped unless 'Press Tab to highlight each item' is on in Safari Settings > Advanced. Set tabToAll to true if you have that setting on.

keyboard._comment: Shortcut that moves focus into the panel, or back to where you were on the page. Escape inside the panel also goes back.

timing._comment: A model, not a measurement. Cost of one stop = secondsPerTab + (speech: words heard / wordsPerMinute * 60, or visualSecondsPerStop if no speech). Words heard = accessible name + spoken role (+ state), capped at maxWordsHeard if set. Activating a link (Enter) costs one secondsPerTab.

profiles.label: Sighted keyboard user
profiles.basis: Key press: the Keystroke-Level Model gives 0.28 s on average (Card, Moran and Newell, 1980); we add time to decide to press again. Finding the focus indicator on screen (0.3 s) is an assumption with no published source.

profiles.label: Screen reader, everyday
profiles.basis: Listens to each full announcement at about 180 words per minute, roughly a default screen reader speech rate (assumption, not from a study).

profiles.label: Screen reader, expert
profiles.basis: Keystroke-Level Model average key press (0.28 s). About 300 words per minute, near the mean listening rate in a large study (Bragg et al., CHI 2018). Experts often cut speech off after a few words and move on; 3 words is an assumption.

roleSpeech._comment: Approximate words a screen reader adds for each role. Real wording differs between NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver.

checks._comment: measureFocus briefly focuses each stop (then restores focus and scroll) to test skip links and sticky headers. probeTabKey sends a synthetic Tab keydown to non-text elements to spot code that cancels Tab.
